ScheduledIntentCreate.title: ScheduledIntentCreate
ScheduledIntentCreate.description:
Request model for creating a new scheduled intent.

Defines a proactive trigger that can fire based on time (cron/interval/once)
or conditions (price/silence/portfolio).

cooldown_hours.title: Cooldown Hours
cooldown_hours.description: Minimum hours between condition-based trigger fires (1-168, default 24)

fire_mode.title: Fire Mode
fire_mode.description: Fire mode: 'once' disables after first successful fire, 'recurring' (default) continues

TriggerCondition.title: TriggerCondition
TriggerCondition.description:
Condition configuration for condition-based triggers (price, silence, portfolio).

Used within ScheduledIntentCreate to define the conditions that must be met.
Fields used depend on trigger_type:
- price: ticker, operator, value OR expression (e.g., "NVDA < 130")
- silence: threshold_hours OR expression (e.g., "inactive_hours > 48")
- portfolio: expression (e.g., "any_holding_change > 5%")

New expression field takes precedence over structured fields when both are provided.

check_interval_minutes.title: Check Interval Minutes
check_interval_minutes.description: Polling interval in minutes for condition-based triggers (min 5). Default: 5 for most triggers, 15 for portfolio triggers.

TriggerSchedule.title: TriggerSchedule
TriggerSchedule.description:
Schedule configuration for time-based triggers (cron, interval, once).

Used within ScheduledIntentCreate to define when a trigger should fire.
Only one of cron, interval_minutes, or trigger_at should be set based on trigger_type.

content.example: User mentioned they prefer morning meetings and work best between 9am-12pm.

ttl_seconds.title: Ttl Seconds
ttl_seconds.description: Optional TTL in seconds, honored on ALL layers (short-term, semantic, long-term, and typed layers). When set, the memory becomes eligible for eviction approximately `ttl_seconds` after creation. Soft contract: a record may linger up to one TTL-sweep cycle past its expiration before deletion. If omitted, short-term records use SHORT_TERM_TTL_SECONDS (default 60 days); all other layers remain immortal.

event_timestamp.title: Event Timestamp
event_timestamp.description: When the event occurred (ISO8601 format). Setting this triggers storage to episodic_memories table.

emotional_state.title: Emotional State
emotional_state.description: Primary emotional state (e.g., 'happy', 'anxious', 'excited'). Setting this triggers storage to emotional_memories table.

trigger_event.title: Trigger Event
trigger_event.description: Event that triggered the emotional state

skill_name.title: Skill Name
skill_name.description: Name of the skill or procedure. Setting this triggers storage to procedural_memories table.

DirectMemoryRequest.title: DirectMemoryRequest
DirectMemoryRequest.description:
Request body for direct memory storage.

Allows clients to store memories directly without LLM extraction.
Supports general memory fields plus optional typed fields (episodic,
emotional, procedural) that trigger routing to specialized storage tables.

content.title: Content
content.description: New memory content. When changed, the embedding is regenerated synchronously. When the new content produces the same content_hash as the stored one, embedding regen is skipped.
content.example: User now prefers afternoon meetings between 2-4pm.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Shallow-merge metadata patch. Keys present here override the stored values; keys absent here are preserved. Use the sentinel value `"__delete__"` to remove a key. System-managed keys (`user_id`, `layer`, `type`, `ttl_epoch`, `timestamp`, `content_hash`, `stored_in_*`, `typed_table_id`) cannot be set or deleted via PATCH metadata; attempts return 422.

layer.title: Layer
layer.description: New memory layer. Allowed flips are between non-typed layers (`short-term` <-> `semantic` <-> `long-term`). Flips into or out of typed-storage layers (`episodic`, `procedural`, `emotional`) return 422 in v1 — delete and recreate instead.

importance.title: Importance
importance.description: New importance score from 0.0 to 1.0. On typed tables that have an importance_score column (episodic_memories), the value is also fanned out.

ttl_seconds.title: Ttl Seconds
ttl_seconds.description: New TTL in seconds. Recomputes `ttl_epoch = now + ttl_seconds`. Pass explicit JSON `null` to clear the stored TTL (immortalize the record). Omit the field entirely to leave the TTL unchanged. Soft-TTL contract: a record may linger up to one TTL-sweep cycle past its expiration before deletion.

PatchMemoryRequest.title: PatchMemoryRequest
PatchMemoryRequest.description:
Request body for ``PATCH /v1/memories/{memory_id}``.

All fields are optional. Omitted fields leave the stored value unchanged.

The ``ttl_seconds`` field uses the ``UNSET`` sentinel scheme so the router
can distinguish between ``{"ttl_seconds": null}`` (clear TTL) and the field
being absent from the request body (leave TTL unchanged). Other fields use
``Optional[T] = None`` because ``None`` is not a meaningful value for
them — supplying ``None`` is equivalent to omitting the key.

Metadata semantics (AC8): shallow merge. Use the string sentinel
``"__delete__"`` as a value to remove a key. System-managed metadata keys
(see ``src/services/_constants.py:SYSTEM_MANAGED_FIELDS``) cannot be
set or deleted via this field; the router returns 422 for any such key.
